submitted.rationale: Index 97 (the equal-thirds Ca/Fe/Mn centroid) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 3e-8 A. The other two measurements were about zero. Every result was near the noise floor, so the library looks weakly active under 3.2 eV light.

rejected.reason: Fe-rich (Fe 0.70), the hematite-like region: measured -1e-8 A. Hematite is stable (MACE hull 0) and absorbs (HSE gap 2.77 eV), but the film gave no photocurrent.
Not measured. MEGNet predicts a gap of about 0 eV for the Mn2O3 corundum analogue, so it is likely a poor photoanode.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts hematite Fe2O3 on the hull, so a stable Fe2O3-based absorber with a gap around 2.1 eV, below the 3.2 eV photon energy, is plausible in the most Fe-rich corner. Index 7 is the most Fe-rich candidate.

Mostly uninformative for this candidate. The HSE gap for Fe2O3 is 2.77 eV, so 3.2 eV photons are absorbed, yet the Fe-rich film (index 7) gave no photocurrent. The bottleneck is probably phase or transport, not absorption. I'm switching to the Ca-rich corner (index 118), where Ca-Fe ferrite phases such as CaFe2O4 and Ca2Fe2O5 may form. This is an exploratory measurement.

This argues against the Mn-rich corner. MEGNet predicts a gap of about 0 eV for the Mn2O3 corundum analogue, so Mn-rich films are likely metallic-like absorbers with fast recombination. Both the Fe-rich (index 7) and Ca-rich (index 118) corners gave zero photocurrent. With one measurement left, I'll test the unexplored ternary centroid (index 97, ~1/3 each), where a mixed Ca–Fe–Mn phase could form.
